questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I study japanese so it had to be Japan

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The host university were really good at supplying us with the information we needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: we were all assigned a tutor who helped us with everything especially in the start

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: it was still a university dorm so it was just assigned to me by the university

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: the cost of going to campus can be very high depending on how far away the dorm is

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: we had 2 weeks to go to classes and choose which ones we wanted. This is quite different from how it is done at my home university so it was very confusing but once we figured it out it was a simple process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: our tutor and the university staff were all very helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got to take all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: For me it was very important that my japanese lessons took priority so i made my schedule after those classes. however this did mean that i did not have a  lot of classes to choose between

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: in my opinion most of the classes (at least the ones taught in english) were lower than danish university level. For the japanese classes you had a lot of choice over which level you wanted to be at

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a bit more lecture based than at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Language Structure
Gender, Culture and Society
Human comparative communication
Upper elementary japanese A + B
Speaking and listening (japanese)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All the english classes were all very interesting, Gender, culture and society provided a very good insight into japanese society which other classes didn't

questions.answer: The host university required us to get additional insurance even though i was already fully insured through my travel insurance

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: transportation was a lot more expecieve than expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there were lots of clubs available to us

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: i didn't end up joining any clubs, but i did go on a lot of trips which i highly recommend

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you go to Kobe university you should definitely go to Rokko Mountain the view from there is amazing. And of course go and see as much of Japan as possible

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was pretty easy for me to adjust to japanese culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I personale found it really hard but it is easiest to gain local friends through your tutor

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I felt like i stood out a lot in public and got a lot of stares as kobe does not have many turists you tend to stand out a lot

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: i loved how quiet and orderly japan was it made it so easy to fit in and just mind your own business. Everyone was also so nice and very helpfull

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would have taken a higher level of japanese than i did as my japanese did not improve as much as i wanted
try to get some japanese friends maybe through your tutor 
try to find a conversation partner to speak japanese with

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: challenge yourself in regards to japanese it will really help you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: i made some really great friend s from different countries and therefore ended up learning more cultures than just the japanese culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: making friends was really hard in the beginning and making good japanese friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
